data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: since
sections.summary: Because; given that; used to introduce a reason or explanation for something.

senses.definition: used to introduce a clause that gives the reason for what is stated in the main clause; because; given that
examples: Since nobody objected, the plan was approved.

answers.answer: Since it was late, we decided to go home.
Since it was late so we decided to go home.
Since was late, we decided to go home.
We decided to go home since it is late yesterday.

sections.question: so that
sections.summary: Used to introduce a clause expressing purpose or intended result; in order that.

senses.definition: used to introduce a clause that expresses the purpose or intended result of the action in the main clause; in order that
examples: He left early so that he could catch the first train.

answers.answer: She spoke clearly so that everyone could understand her.
She spoke clearly so everyone could understand her.
She spoke clearly so that could understand her.
She spoke clearly so that everyone can understood her.

sections.question: though
sections.summary: In spite of the fact that; used to introduce a contrast; similar to 'although'.

senses.definition: used to introduce a clause that contrasts with or qualifies the main clause; in spite of the fact that; a slightly less formal alternative to 'although'
examples: The food was good, though the service was very slow.

answers.answer: The task was difficult, though we managed to finish it.
Though the task was difficult, but we managed to finish it.
The task was difficult though but we managed to finish it.
The task was difficult, though managed to finish it.

sections.question: unless
sections.summary: Except if; only if not; used to introduce a condition that must be met to prevent something.

senses.definition: except if; used to introduce the only condition under which the situation in the main clause will not happen or is not true
examples: You will miss the show unless you leave right now.

answers.answer: You won't pass unless you study harder.
You won't pass unless you will study harder.
Unless you study harder you won't pass it, but.
You won't pass unless studying harder.

sections.question: whereas
sections.summary: Used to contrast two different facts or situations; while on the other hand.

senses.definition: used to introduce a fact that contrasts with what is stated in the main clause; while on the other hand; used to highlight a difference between two things
examples: My brother loves sport, whereas I prefer reading books.

answers.answer: She prefers tea, whereas I prefer coffee.
She prefers tea whereas but I prefer coffee.
She prefers tea, whereas prefer coffee.
She prefers tea whereas to I prefer coffee.

sections.question: while
sections.summary: During the time that; at the same time as; also used to introduce a contrast.

senses.definition: during the time that something else is happening; at the same time as; also used to introduce a contrast between two situations
examples: She listened to music while she was doing her homework.

answers.answer: While I was cooking, he was setting the table.
While I was cooking he was setting, the table.
While was cooking, he was setting the table.
He was setting the table while I cooking.
